title: A plate v1 left `generating` is never rendered by render-plates, and three places say a job holds it
body:
## Summary
needsPlate (packages/producers/src/frames/define.ts:40-42) skips a `generating` plate because it "belongs to a job in flight", but no v2 writer ever sets a plate to generating; such a plate (v1-imported) is never owed by render-plates.

## Description
packages/producers/src/frames/define.ts:40-42 needsPlate excludes `generating`; its doc says the plate belongs to a job in flight. The same claim is in app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureFrames.ts:100-101 and in the mutant `frames-rebuys-plate-in-flight` (tests/mutants-unit/registry.ts: "A batch re-buys a plate another job is rendering"). Measured: the v2 tree has 0 writers of plate state `generating` (lib/producers/frames.ts lands only `ready` or `refused`; grep over lib, app, packages, workers). The state survives only on records v1 wrote (lib/frames/frames.ts:90-94: the v1 browser saved a render's receipt key while generating, so a reload could re-issue under it and be handed the pixels already paid for). So a v1 plate stuck at generating is skipped by the batch act forever and is reachable only by an explicit render-plate on its unit. Fixed looks like one of: owe a `generating` plate that carries a receipt and re-issue under that key (no new spend when the server already settled), or keep the skip and say the true reason in all three places. The choice touches spend, hence not Lane A.

## Flow
- import a v1 project whose frames record holds a plate at state generating
- run render-plates (DRY) -> 0 units for that plate; the act's label (fixtureFrames owes) counts it as not owed
- fix: decide re-issue-under-receipt vs skip; update needsPlate, owes, the mutant's why and steps-frames.test.ts:24 together

## Expected impact
An imported project's stuck plates either render through the batch act or are named honestly. Could break: a re-issue whose receipt the server no longer holds buys a fresh image.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the batch act's skip rule matches who can actually hold a generating plate
Before: v2 writers of plate state generating: 0; places claiming a job holds one: 3
After: either 1 path renders a receipt-carrying generating plate without new spend, or 0 false claims
Method: simulation - grep of writers and a read of the v1 receipt rule; the re-issue path needs a DRY render-plates job over a generating plate in tests/next-server/producer-step-frames.test.ts, not built
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/producers/src/frames/define.ts:40 /** ... A plate the batch is `generating` belongs to a job in flight and is not bought twice. */
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureFrames.ts:100 A `generating` plate belongs to a job in flight
lib/producers/frames.ts:300-302 lands state refused | ready only
grep '"generating"' lib app packages workers -> type declarations, a kit specimen, lib/cut/deriveTimeline.ts label; 0 writers
instrument: a DRY render-plates case in tests/next-server/producer-step-frames.test.ts over a unit whose plate is generating with a receipt: units planned for it (0 before)

title: An adopt's palette read is bought without the re-check the style header promises
body:
## Summary
packages/producers/src/style/define.ts:22-23 says the world is re-checked before each paid call; lib/producers/style.ts palette (the adopt's one paid recognize) never reads the style row, so an adopt of a style that gained a block since its receipt pays the read and only the landing refuses.

## Description
The proofs path re-checks: lib/producers/style.ts:136 compares the block digest with req.digest and stops before the image. The adopt path does not: palette (lib/producers/style.ts:212) reads the foundry catalogue def and calls adoptionDraft, which spends the recognize call; the style's rev and block are checked only at land (adoptStyleIn). A second adopt (or a hand-written block) between the receipt and the drive therefore buys a palette read whose landing then refuses. Fixed: palette reads the style row first and returns the work's refusal (`already has a look`, or a moved rev) before the paid call, as actRefusal in lib/producers/styleLaunch.ts states it at the receipt.

## Flow
- launch adopt on style X (receipt at rev n)
- write a block on X (another adopt landing first)
- drive the first adopt -> palette pays the recognize read; land refuses
- fix: palette re-reads X and refuses before adoptionDraft

## Expected impact
No paid read is bought for an adopt that cannot land. Could break: nothing for a style untouched since its receipt.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience/spend - every paid call of a style job is preceded by the re-check
Before: paid steps with a pre-call re-check: 1 of 2 (proofs yes, palette no)
After: 2 of 2
Method: simulation - read of both step bodies; the fix is in lib/producers/style.ts, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/producers/style.ts:136 if (now !== req.digest) return fatal("conflict", ...)
lib/producers/style.ts:212-217 palette: getCatalogue -> adoptionDraft (paid) with no style row read
packages/producers/src/style/define.ts:22 The world is re-checked before each paid call
instrument: a case in tests/next-server/style-real.test.ts: an adopt whose style gains a block after the receipt -> the recognize engine is called 0 times (1 before)
